title: The Trust Paradox: Why 4.2 Stars Beats 5.0
excerpt: Purchase intent peaks between 4.2 and 4.5 stars, not at 5.0, because users are intuitive Bayesian reasoners who read volume as validity and perfection as manipulation. The UX takeaway is to design for predictability: users are not looking for perfect, they are looking for proven.

slides.headline: Why 4.2★ beats 5.0★
slides.standfirst: The science of social proof in UX.

body.text: A large sample size filters out outliers and statistical noise.
We update our trust based on the strength of evidence.
1,000 data points create a stronger **prior** than 5 perfect ones.

slides.eyebrow: The "Too Good to Be True" Effect
slides.headline: Perfection triggers skepticism.

body.text: Research shows purchase intent peaks between **4.2 and 4.5 stars**.
Above 4.5, users suspect manipulation or data censorship.
Users aren't looking for **perfect**, they are looking for **proven**.

callout.text: Is your product's rating authentic, or just lucky?
